operative_text.controlling:
2.29(1)  Subject to rule 2.31, a lawyer or firm of lawyers may
withdraw as lawyer of record by
(a) serving on the client and each of the other parties a notice
of withdrawal in Form 4 that states
(i) the client’s last known address, and
(ii) that on the expiry of 10 days after the date on which
the affidavit of service of the notice is filed, the
withdrawing lawyer will no longer be the lawyer of
record,
and
(b) filing an affidavit of service of the notice.
(2)  The withdrawal of the lawyer of record takes effect 10 days
after the affidavit of service of the notice is filed.
(3)  The address of the party stated in the notice of withdrawal is
the party’s address for service after the lawyer of record withdraws
unless another address for service is provided or the Court
otherwise orders.
(4)  The Court may on application order that a lawyer need not
disclose the last known address of a client and instead may provide
an alternative address for service for the client in a notice of
withdrawal served under this rule where the Court considers it
necessary to protect the safety and well-being of the client.
(5)  An application under subrule (4) may be made without notice.

BOOK_A.title: Withdrawal of Lawyer of Record
BOOK_A.related_provisions: 2.31 (withdrawal after trial scheduled) ; 2.32 (lawyer ceasing to practice) ; 9.2 (duty to prepare orders); 11.17 (service on lawyer of record) ; 11.18 (service on self-represented person).
BOOK_A.commentary:
This commentary is mostly about the law. For some advice and practical tips, see Côté,
Systematic Advocacy, Chapter 2, Part Q (Juriliber 2017).
Counsel can withdraw and bill for work to date, if his legal advice is rejected by his client.¹
If counsel’s withdrawal or dismissal causes a mistrial, that client should pay his opponent’s
costs of the abortive trial, though usually he should not lose his suit if he does not pay them
promptly.²
That a solicitor later withdrew does not affect the validity of earlier service upon him instead of
personal service upon his client.³
Some provinces require leave of the court before a lawyer can withdraw. Alberta wisely does
not require that in civil cases. A lawyer cannot withdraw when that would mean serious harm to
the client, but that is normally conﬁned to times shortly before a scheduled trial or appeal.⁴
In a
criminal case, a lawyer does need leave to get off the record.⁵
Few lawyers follow all the necessary steps to take themselves off the record. The lawyer
remains solicitor of record until the 11th day after the last of those steps is complete,⁶
which
produces many artiﬁcial legal results and much uncertainty. The necessary steps are that
(a) the notice contain the right wording, especially the notice under R.2.29(1) (c) and the last
known address of the client, and
(b) it be properly served on all the necessary persons, and
(c) afﬁdavits of such service be ﬁled.⁷
There was some discrepancy between the body and backer of a notice of ceasing to act. It
was interpreted as meaning that it did not take effect until 10 days after ﬁling evidence proving
service on the former client, so service on him at the new address was ineffective (as he claimed
not to have got it).⁸
A lawyer who is unable to locate his client may not be able to cease to act, because he cannot
give the client notice.⁹

On the lawyer’s duty to approve the form of an order after ceasing to act, see R.9.2n.

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.555. It came from 1944 C. R.646, much of which came from Sask. R.16 (pt. ), and Ont.1928 R.389, 1883 Eng. O.7 r.3, and Judic. Ord. s.11, and 1914 Rr.463, and 563a.
Ashton & Co. v. Pullishy (CA 1 Dec) [1997] AUD 277.
Hrycoy Est. v. Hrycoy Est. (CA 1999) 244 AR 338.
N. -S. Trade & Inv. v. Aquanorth Farms 2002 ABQB 553, 321 AR 140, revg (M) 2002 ABQB 74. See R. 11.17.
See further the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part J.4.

R. v. Kong 2003 ABQB 192, 12 Alta LR(4th) 187. The court’s power to force the lawyer to remain and act is sparingly used, and a statement that the problem is either ethics or non-payment, is not gone behind: R. (Lilles) v. Cunningham 2010 SCC 10, [2010] 1 SCR 331. It was not done where a long jury trial was 2 months away and the only problem was nonpayment of fees: Kong and Cunningham cases. There is a discussion of whether it is sufﬁcient ground to get such leave that the lawyer has lost contact with the client in Re A. L.2003 ABQB 905, 345 AR 201. See further R.2.24n. A.
Josza v. Josza 2010 ABCA 282, [2010] AR Uned 409, 2010 CarswellAlta 1940 (Sep 30).
See the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part J.2.
Neddow v. Weidemann 2008 ABQB 378, 92 Alta LR(4th) 331.

BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: probable wrong subrule reference: 'especially the notice under R.2.29(1) (c) and the last known address of the client'. Official 2.29(1) has only clauses (a) and (b); the notice's contents are in 2.29(1)(a)(i) (last known address) and (ii) (10-day statement). Left as printed. Checked: the last sentence ('On the lawyer's duty ... see R.9.2n.') is printed at the top of p.2-65 before the 2.30 heading and belongs to 2.29; footnotes p.2-63 fn 4 and p.2-64 fns 1-9 consecutive; 'Kong and Cunningham cases' (fn 5) resolve within the same footnote. Case-name variant: fn 5 'R. (Lilles) v. Cunningham' and 2.24 p.2-50 fn 3 'Cunningham v. Lilles (R. v. Cunningham)' are the same 2010 SCC 10. 4th pass: the statement 'Some provinces require leave of the court before a lawyer can withdraw. Alberta wisely does not require that in civil cases' must be read with official rule 2.31 - after a trial date is scheduled, a notice of withdrawal needs the Court's permission or has no effect. Book A's next sentence (serious harm, 'shortly before a scheduled trial') points that way but does not cite 2.31.

BOOK_B.title: Withdrawal of lawyer of record

commentary.text: Rule 2.29 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 2.29. How Not to Withdraw as Counsel In Baron Real Estate Investments Ltd. v. Edmonton (Subdivision and Development Appeal Board), 2018 ABCA 67, 2018 CarswellAlta 301, a lawyer purported to withdraw as counsel of record by delivering a letter to the Court of Appeal on the day of a scheduled hearing before the Court. Justice Wakeling pointed out the error in that procedure. 22 Counsel for Baron Real Estate did not appear on Wednesday. Instead, counsel informed the Court in a letter received by the Registry at 9:39 am that he withdrew as lawyer of record. 23 A lawyer does not withdraw as lawyer of record by delivering a letter to the court. Rule 2.29(1) of the Alberta Rules of Court23 provides an unambiguous protocol. The lawyer who wishes to withdraw must file a notice of withdrawal and serve it on the parties and file an affidavit of service. Rule 2.29(2) provides that “[t]he withdrawal of the lawyer of record takes effect 10 days after the affidavit of service of the notice is filed”. 24 As a result, Baron Real Estate's lawyer of record was not in attendance when his client's application was called. Given that Baron Real Estate is a corporation, neither its officers nor shareholders were entitled to speak on its behalf ….
